Read out of saint.gr's line for 24 Απριλίου, «Άγιοι Πασικράτης και Βαλεντίων», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог's heading for 24. април ст. ст., „Св. муч. Пасикрат и Валентин.“, with „Св.“ and the one rank word муч., which stands over both names, left off. The heading gives no city: Durostorum, which this corpus's English name keeps, is the Greek calendar's and is nowhere in this entry. No other folder in this corpus holds this form in any language.

Read out of the title on the name link behind the line for 24 апреля ст. ст., name page 1742, «Пасикрат Доростольский, мч.», with the rank abbreviation after the comma left off; the day’s own line gives only the genitive «Пасикрата» and no city. Measured against the gate’s own key function before it was written: 'доростольскии пасикрат' has no other holder in the corpus.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 24 апреля ст. ст. — «Мчч. Пасикрата и Валентина (228).»
source.note: The day’s third entry, a line naming two men, of whom this is the first. The name link, page 1742, is titled «Пасикрат Доростольский, мч.» and gives the city, which the line does not; both it and the life head «День памяти: 24 апреля» and no other day. THE LINE AND THE LIFE DISAGREE ON THE YEAR BY SIXTY, AND `dates` WAS NOT CHANGED. The line heads the pair «(228)»; life927 ends «Оба мученика были усечены мечом (+ 288)». The two differ in one digit and the earlier of them is far outside the persecution the account describes, so the likelihood is a slip on the day line; but a year is one of the nine things a machine may not decide and this folder’s interval, 275 to 297 off saint.gr, agrees with neither. Both readings are set out in the life. REPORTED TO THE AUTHOR. What the life does give and nothing else did: he was twenty-two years old. The day page prints no hymn under his name. Not checked: azbyka.ru.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 24 aprilie — «Sfântul Mucenic Pasicrat din Durostorum»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 24ης Απριλίου — «Άγιοι Πασικράτης και Βαλεντίων»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 24 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing and the same day the Romanian calendar keeps them. The Greek makes them soldiers of Durostorum in Lower Moesia under a prefect Aulozanes, arrested for rebuking the worshippers of the idols and for confessing Christ true God, urged to sacrifice to Apollo, and beheaded in 297 — Passicrates at twenty-two, Valention at thirty; it adds the scene of Passicrates's brother coming to the prison and advising him to offer at least a little incense and save himself, and Passicrates driving him off. **This folder had no `dates` and now has both years**, taken from the page's headings «Αγιος Βαλεντιων (267 - 297)» and «Αγιος Πασικρατης (275 - 297)», which are the ages the text gives worked back from 297. The day's line spells the second name Βαλεντίων, and the corpus's English form is Valentine. It prints no hymn and names no relic.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 07.05.2026 (24. април ст. ст.) — „Св. муч. Пасикрат и Валентин.“

attestations.note: A SECOND DAY ON THIS CHURCH, ADDED 5 October 2026. **THE BOOK CONTRADICTS ITSELF ACROSS ITS OWN TWO DAYS, AND BY SEVENTY-FOUR YEARS.** `BRIEF.md` §4 allows a reader to write a second-day note on a row that is already `venerated`, under `replace_venerated: true`, and **the row is copied back byte for byte** — same day, same month, same source, same year — **with the note added and nothing else changed**. The Prologue keeps this man **twice**: on the Julian 24 April, headed „Св. муч. Пасикрат и Валентин.“, where it says the two were beheaded together „око 228. год.“, and again here on the Julian 25 May, where it says the company suffered „око 302. године“. **It is the same pair and demonstrably so, because the same brother appears in both**: the apostate Папијан, who in the 24 April entry is urged on Pasicrates by the judge and in this one comes to him himself. **So this is not two men but one book with two answers**, which is the reading made for `basiliscus-of-amasea` on 22 May, where the Prologue’s own 3 March and 22 May entries told his death two ways. **No second row was made and no day was moved**: one attestation row per church is the schema, this church’s row stays on the Julian 24 April, and he does not render on the 25 May. **And `dates` is untouched.** The folder holds a `death` of 297 off doxologia and saint.gr; the Prologue’s two guesses, 228 and 302, straddle it, and widening to 228–302 on the strength of two approximations the same book makes against itself would put a seventy-four-year interval on the folder in place of a year two other calendars agree on. **It is recorded here and left for the author.** The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of the 23, 24 and 25 May is. The 25 May heading is „Свети мученици Пасикрат, Валентион, Јулије и други“ and the 25 May entry is the one that names the company: Roman soldiers who suffered for Christ at Durostorum. **New from it, and not on any other page read for him**: that **when his brother Папијан, who had fallen away from Christ out of fear, came to him and began urging him to deny Christ and stay alive, Pasicrates answered „Иди од мене, ти ми ниси брат!“** — go from me, you are not my brother. The 24 April entry has the same brother but has the **judge** urge him, and this hard sentence is only here; there the mother encourages him and here she is not mentioned. **He gains no new name form**: «Пасикрат» is already stored off the 24 April heading and the 25 May heading prints the identical string, measured with `foldchk.py`, which returns `[('passicrates-of-durostorum', 'sr')]` and nothing else. **Папијан gains no folder and no row**: a brother is a kinship the body narrates, which is the test that owes a row, **but no calendar read for this corpus keeps him** — `ls saints | grep -i papia` returns only the four Papiases, who are other men — and by the coordinator’s third ruling nothing is minted for an apostate the book names to contrast him. He is in the prose, unlinked. **THREE NEW `related` ROWS, ALL RECIPROCAL.** This folder related only to `valentine-of-durostorum`. The 25 May entry narrates one martyrdom for five men, which is the test that owes a row, so `julius-the-veteran`, `nicander-of-durostorum` and `marcian-of-durostorum` are added here and this folder is added on each of theirs. `hesychius-of-durostorum` is NOT added: he is in `julius-the-veteran`’s life off saint.gr, **this entry does not name him**, and a row is owed for what the body narrates. `types` untouched, both corroborated. No `locations`. No hymn.

birth.note: saint.gr heads him «Αγιος Πασικράτης (275 - 297)», and its text gives his age at death as twenty-two in the year 297.

death.note: saint.gr: «Τότε και οι δύο αποκεφαλίστηκαν, σε ηλικία, ο μεν Πασικράτης 22 ετών, ο δε Βαλεντίων 30, το έτος 297 μ.Χ.»
